articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Oviedo vs Sporting
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Oviedo y Sporting en el Carlos Tartiere correspondiente a la jornada 7 de LaLiga Hypermotion 26-27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Oviedo y Sporting en el Carlos Tartiere correspondiente a la jornada 7 de LaLiga Hypermotion 26-27
articles.body: El Oviedo afronta el derbi asturiano después de caer en su visita al Sabadell, un resultado que prolonga una dinámica irregular en su regreso a Segunda División. El conjunto carbayón suma dos victorias, dos empates y dos derrotas en las seis primeras jornadas y ocupa actualmente la decimotercera posición. Ahora tendrá la oportunidad de reencontrarse con la victoria ante su afición en un Carlos Tartiere que vivirá uno de los partidos más esperados de la temporada. Favorito para el partido entre Oviedo y Sporting El Sporting llega al derbi con mejores sensaciones después de imponerse al Andorra en la última jornada y poner fin a una racha de dos derrotas consecutivas. El conjunto rojiblanco marcha noveno en la clasificación... aunque solamente está a un punto de los puestos de 'playoffs', por lo que un triunfo en el Carlos Tartiere podría permitirle acercarse todavía más a la zona alta. Las casas de apuestas conceden el favoritismo al Oviedo: Codere ofrece una cuota de 2.00 por su victoria, 3.00 por el empate y 4.10 por el triunfo del Sporting. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción a tener en cuenta dentro de las apuestas deportivas, aunque las estadísticas recientes apuntan hacia un encuentro con dificultades para ver goles en las dos porterías. El Oviedo solamente ha cumplido este pronóstico en uno de sus cinco últimos partidos. Exactamente, el mismo registro que presenta el Sporting en sus cinco compromisos más recientes. Estos datos reflejan la tendencia de ambos conjuntos a protagonizar encuentros en los que al menos uno de los dos equipos se queda sin marcar. Codere ofrece una cuota de 2.05 por el 'sí' y de 1.70 por el 'no'. Primer equipo en marcar El Oviedo parte con ventaja en este mercado pese a que sus registros recientes no son especialmente contundentes a la hora de adelantarse en el marcador. El conjunto carbayón solamente ha comenzado ganando en dos de sus cinco últimos encuentros, mientras que el Sporting lo ha conseguido en tres de los cinco más recientes. Codere paga a 1.72 que el Oviedo marque primero, frente a los 2.55 que ofrece por el Sporting, mientras que la opción de que no haya goles alcanza una cuota de 7.00. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Las estadísticas de los dos equipos apuntan con bastante claridad hacia un derbi con pocos goles. En solamente dos de los cinco últimos partidos del Oviedo se han superado los 2.5 tantos totales, mientras que en el caso del Sporting esta barrera únicamente se ha alcanzado en uno de sus cinco encuentros más recientes. La tendencia goleadora de ambos conjuntos invita a esperar un marcador corto en el Carlos Tartiere. Codere ofrece una cuota de 4.75 por que haya más de 2.5 goles y de 1.12 por que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos.

articles.title: A Cristiano se le resiste
articles.standfirst: Espera poner fin a una racha de tres partidos sin marcar en un encuentro en el que Monopoly no da favorita a Portugal contra Noruega
articles.summary: Espera poner fin a una racha de tres partidos sin marcar en un encuentro en el que Monopoly no da favorita a Portugal contra Noruega
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo está inmerso en una carrera contrarreloj hacia los 1.000 goles para coronar su carrera y ya está encarando la recta final de un desafío histórico. Al portugués tan sólo le faltan 21 tantos para alcanzar esa cifra redonda, pero el 980 se le está resistiendo más de lo habitual: suma tres goles en este inicio de temporada... aunque enlaza tres partidos sin marcar entre los disputados con Al Nassr y Portugal. Una sequía poco habitual en él. Su último compromiso con la Selección terminó, además, con una circunstancia poco habitual. Portugal derrotó a Gales en el estreno de la Nations League gracias a un gol de Joao Félix... pero Jorge Jesus decidió sustituir a Cristiano cuando todavía quedaban más de 20 minutos por disputarse y con la frustración de ver que el VAR le había anulado su gol. Se espera que el luso vuelva a ser de la partida ante Noruega: un encuentro en el que su acierto de cara a portería puede resultar determinante para su equipo. Monopoly refleja la igualdad del duelo con cuotas de 2.45 para el triunfo noruego, 3.75 para el empate y 2.50 para la victoria de Portugal. El próximo partido se presenta, por tanto, como una nueva oportunidad para que Cristiano vuelva a encontrar el camino del gol y reactive su persecución hacia el millar. El desafío llega, además, ante una Noruega que exigirá mucho más a la vigente campeona de la Nations League. Portugal es la única selección que ha conseguido conquistar dos ediciones del torneo y ambas llevan la firma de su gran estrella. Cristiano fue protagonista en los títulos de 2019 y 2025, consagrándose como la pieza fundamental en los éxitos del país a lo largo de esta última década Las apuestas deportivas también reflejan, eso sí, que Portugal no parte esta vez entre las grandes favoritas para volver a levantar el trofeo. Monopoly sitúa su cuota en 8.0, por encima de Francia (4.0), España (4.0), Alemania (5.5) e Inglaterra (6.0). El escenario obliga a los portugueses a demostrar que están en posición de competir por un tercer título y, especialmente, a encontrar en Cristiano al jugador capaz de marcar las diferencias en los momentos decisivos. Las mejores casas de apuestas estarán muy pendientes de la actuación del delantero en esta nueva cita. Cristiano sabe que cada partido cuenta en una carrera hacia una cifra que parecía inalcanzable hace apenas unos años... y que ahora está a sólo 21 goles. Ante Noruega, tendrá una nueva oportunidad para acabar con esta pequeña sequía y acercarse al 980. A sus 41 años, el reto de los 1.000 sigue más vivo que nunca.

articles.title: Wild USC-Oregon fan fight erupts in stands after Dante Moore hit — with an ironic twist
articles.summary: A USC fan wearing No. 8 jersey traded punches with an Oregon fan at the Coliseum after Desman Stephens II’s brutal hit knocked Dante Moore out of the game.
articles.body:
Once again, "Fight On!" was taken a little too literally Saturday night at the Coliseum.

As Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was being tended to by medical personnel following a brutal hit that sent him to a nearby hospital, two USC fans staged their own heavyweight bout in the stands during the Trojans' 41-27 loss to the 20th-ranked Ducks .

And you almost couldn't script the irony.

One USC fan was wearing a No. 8 jersey — the same number worn by Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II, whose forearm shot to Moore's head in the second quarter got him ejected for targeting.

Video of the altercation shows the two fans trading haymakers while spectators scrambled out of the way, watched or pulled out their phones. A woman eventually joined the chaos, appearing to throw her drink toward the USC fan wearing the jersey while attempting to restrain the other person.

"I remember my first fight!" one bystander can be heard yelling.

The whole fracas lasted roughly 20 seconds before others finally separated the two men.

All the while, the far corner of the video provided a sobering backdrop: Moore was still on the field being transferred from a stretcher to a gurney before being taken away by ambulance.

Stephens' hit had already ignited tempers below. Oregon players confronted him immediately after the play, USC players rushed in and a pushing-and-shoving scrum followed .

The hostility apparently survived the final whistle. The Athletic's Ira Gorawara captured video of USC and Oregon players involved in another scuffle in the Coliseum tunnel as the teams headed toward their locker rooms after the game.

The fact that all of this was caused by a No. 8 on the field and another fight broke out with a fan wearing No. 8 in the stands led to some interesting comments as social media noticed the coincidence.

"Buddy was in the stands too?!?!?" one commenter wrote.

"How many No. 8s on SC getting DQd at the game?" another joked.

It marked the second fight involving fans in the Coliseum stands in USC's past two home games.

At this rate, "Fight On!" is starting to sound less like a school slogan and more like an instruction manual.

articles.title: Asian Games: Abhay Singh wins silver after spirited fight in men's squash final
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Abhay Singh claimed the silver medal in the men’s singles squash event at the Asian Games 2026, going down 0–3 to Malaysia’s Ng Eain
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Abhay Singh claimed the silver medal in the men’s singles squash event at the Asian Games 2026, going down 0–3 to Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the gold-medal match on Sunday. The Indian stayed competitive in the opening game before the world No. 17 took control, winning 11–9, 11–5, 11–5 to secure the title.World No. 26 Abhay, who had advanced to the final without major difficulty, was bidding to add another chapter to India’s strong history in men’s singles squash at the continental showpiece. But Ng’s consistency and ability to respond to the Indian’s attacking play proved decisive.The silver gives India another medal in squash, with attention now turning to the women’s singles final, where Anahat Singh is set to face Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAbhay pushes Ng in a close opening gameThe final began with both players trading points, as Abhay looked to put pressure on Ng with his attacking shots. The Malaysian held a narrow 4–3 advantage in the early exchanges, but the Indian stayed close and continued to find ways to challenge his opponent.Abhay produced one of the standout moments of the opening game with a clever change of angle at the last moment. With Ng anticipating the shot to go in another direction, Abhay’s adjustment caught the Malaysian off guard and kept the Indian within reach at 8–7.Ng, however, managed the closing stages better to take the first game 11–9. The narrow margin left Abhay with reason to believe he could turn the contest around, but the Malaysian carried the momentum into the second.Malaysian takes charge to seal goldNg raised his level in the second game, taking it 11–5 to move within one game of the gold medal. Abhay faced the challenge of winning three consecutive games to overturn the deficit, but the Malaysian continued to dictate the rallies and limit the Indian’s opportunities.Abhay made a bright start to the third game, moving 4–2 ahead and briefly suggesting a possible fightback. Ng responded quickly, though, and gradually reclaimed the lead. The Malaysian moved ahead 6–5, with Abhay still within a point, but Ng’s steady play helped him close out the game 11–5 and complete the straight-games victory.The result brought Abhay’s run to a close with a silver medal, while Ng added the Asian Games men’s singles title to his campaign.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Three matches in 24 hours! PV Sindhu criticises Asian Games badminton schedule
articles.summary: PV Sindhu has criticised the badminton schedule at the Asian Games after playing three singles matches in less than 24 hours.
articles.body: PV Sindhu has criticised the badminton schedule at the Asian Games after playing three singles matches in less than 24 hours.The Indian shuttler played twice on Saturday, with her third-round match finishing after midnight. She was back on court on Sunday afternoon for her quarterfinal against China's Chen Yufei, which she lost."Not really, because the scheduling was not really well organised is what I feel," said Sindhu when asked if she had ever played two matches in any major championships earlier.The two-time Olympic medallist said the short gap between matches left little time for recovery."We literally slept really late and then coming back in the morning (on Sunday), playing two matches in a day. Recovery is the most important priority."'You need to recover'Sindhu said the challenge was not only about preparing mentally for another match. The physical recovery between matches was equally important."It's more than mentally preparing, you need to recover. Even though you think you are doing good, physically you might not be able to go there or you might not be able to play."She said the lack of recovery becomes more visible during long rallies."When there are long rallies, definitely yes, recovery. When you had a good thing, you would automatically (go) but your legs don't move."But I think apart from that it was a good game overall but it's just that the scheduling should have been a bit better."Unnati Hooda also expressed her disappointment with the scheduling after players were required to play more than one match in a day."I will not blame my loss (in quarterfinals) to that but the scheduling could have been managed better."Sindhu questions absence of Hawk-EyeSindhu also felt the absence of Hawk-Eye on Court 4 made things difficult during her quarterfinal.Some line calls were close, but there was no player challenge available because Hawk-Eye had been installed only on show courts 1 and 2 at the Ichinomiya Gymnasium Hall."There were no cameras here. That was really sad. I felt that 2-3 shots were on the line. In the quarter-finals in the Asian Games, there should have been a camera is what I feel. Because these are the crucial matches."Sindhu said the review system can make a difference, especially when a close line call goes against a player."If you get that point, it is good. You have upper hand. You are playing with the cameras, playing with reviews."We can challenge it or if that's your point, you have a one point advantage. Sometimes an opponent is not able to move and the shuttle falls there and the line judge gives out. And you challenge, you get a point."So it's an advantage in a way. In the second game, I felt 2-3 shots were clear. But the line judge, you can't do anything about it."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Harita Bhadra secured a hard-fought bronze medal in the women’s 200m at the Asian Games 2026 on Sunday, edging Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido

Indonesia’s Shanti Pereira won the gold in 22.78s, while China’s 100m champion Yujie Chen took silver with a timing of 22.93s.The bronze was India’s ninth athletics medal at the ongoing Games, taking the country’s track and field haul to four silver and five bronze medals. Her best effort stood at 6.49m at that stage of the competition.Tejaswin Shankar was also still in medal contention in the decathlon, sitting third with only the final event remaining.Few minutes later, India’s Animesh Kujur finished fifth in the men’s 200m final after clocking 20.80 seconds. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ancy Sojan came agonisingly close to giving India its first athletics gold at the Asian Games 2026, but had to settle for silver after China’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ancy Sojan came agonisingly close to giving India its first athletics gold at the Asian Games 2026, but had to settle for silver after China’s Yingying Huang produced a decisive final jump in the women’s long jump in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Sunday. Shaili Singh also missed out on a medal, finishing fourth after China’s Mengyi Tan edged her out with her last attempt.Ancy had taken the lead with a jump of 6.53m in her fifth attempt, but Huang responded with 6.55m in the final round to snatch the gold by just two centimetres. Ancy’s final effort was 6.49m.Shaili, meanwhile, was sitting third with 6.42m after five attempts. But Tan produced 6.46m in her final jump to move into bronze-medal position and push the Indian to fourth.Ancy’s silver took India’s athletics tally to 10 medals — five silver and five bronze — while the country continued to wait for its first gold in track and field. India’s overall medal count stood at 34, with four gold, 15 silver and 15 bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleHuang’s final jump denies Ancy goldAncy began strongly, opening with a jump of 6.49m to establish herself among the medal contenders. Huang matched that distance in her fifth attempt, setting up a close contest between the two.The Indian then raised the bar with a 6.53m effort in the fifth round to move into the lead. With the gold within reach, Ancy needed to hold on through the final attempts.Huang had other plans. The Chinese jumper delivered 6.55m with her last attempt, overtaking Ancy and securing the title. Ancy could not improve on her leading mark, managing 6.49m in her final jump, and finished just short of gold.For Shaili, the final round brought a similarly painful twist. Her 6.42m had placed her third after five attempts, but Tan’s 6.46m effort pushed her off the podium.Harita’s bronze earlier in the dayEarlier on Sunday, Harita Bhadra had won bronze in the women’s 200m after edging Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido in a photo-finish. Harita clocked 23.20 seconds, just 0.01 seconds ahead of Ido’s 23.21s.Indonesia’s Shanti Pereira won gold in 22.78s, while China’s 100m champion Yujie Chen took silver in 22.93s. The other Indian in the final, Unnathi Aiyappa Bolland, finished sixth in 23.46s.More events still offer medal chances: India remained in contention for further medals in athletics on Sunday. articles.title: Chess Olympiad: Savitha Shri heroics bring medal; Arjun Erigaisi turns hero as India bag silver in open section
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chess came to the Baskar household not through Savitha Shri but through her older brother, Mugesh, whom their father had originally set out to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chess came to the Baskar household not through Savitha Shri but through her older brother, Mugesh, whom their father had originally set out to build a chess career around. Savitha's own interest came from watching him play.By the time both children were training under Chennai-based coach RB Ramesh, a decision had to be made, with the expense of chess becoming heavier with each passing day. The family couldn't sustain two chess careers, and Mugesh stepped back after the eighth standard while Savitha kept going.Her father, Baskar, an electrician in Singapore at the time, eventually quit that job entirely and returned to India to support her career, a transition so difficult that the family once pawned his gold jewellery to fund a national tournament entry fee."Taking that decision was very difficult," Baskar told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction after it was announced that Savitha would represent the Indian women's team at the 2026 Chess Olympiad. On Sunday, in Samarkand, that sacrifice produced its biggest payoff yet.Savitha's clutch draw saves the dayRound 11 began well enough for India's women, with Koneru Humpy wrapping up a win in just 24 moves. But the match swung quickly. Divya Deshmukh lost her game, and Vantika Agrawal settled for a draw, leaving everything to play for on the fourth board.A draw there would have been enough to keep India's medal hopes alive. For a long stretch, it looked like even that might not arrive as Savitha found herself worse against Meri Arabidze, and for a while it felt as though India might finish this Olympiad without a medal at all.She didn't let it happen. Playing black in a Queen's Gambit-flavoured middlegame, Savitha came under sustained pressure as Arabidze's pieces grew more active and her own king was pushed around the board.Through a marathon 83-move battle, one that swung through a queen-and-rook middlegame before resolving into a rook endgame, Savitha defended with remarkable patience, meeting check after check and repeatedly finding the only moves that kept her position alive.The game eventually settled into a drawn rook ending, with Arabidze unable to force a breakthrough despite repeated tries, and the point was shared after 83 moves.It was, fittingly, Savitha who once again delivered when India needed her most.The match itself ended 2-2. Humpy's win and Savitha's draw offset Divya's loss and Vantika's own draw, and India's women closed the tournament on 17 points, finishing third.China ran away with gold on 20 points, while Kazakhstan's own draw in the final round was enough to edge them to silver on 18.Erigaisi turns hero, India survive on tiebreak for open silverIf the women's story was about redemption, the open section has something better for you. Arjun Erigaisi had endured a torrid start to this Olympiad, losing to lower-rated Thai opposition on the opening day while filling in for a rested Praggnanandhaa on Board 1.What followed was a fairly ordinary campaign by his standards. One win, against Spain, followed by six straight draws. Nobody was quite prepared for what came in the final round.Playing black against veteran Peter Leko, Erigaisi found himself in a long, grinding Ruy Lopez battle that stretched deep into the game with pieces trading down slowly rather than any early fireworks.Both sides manoeuvred for what felt like an age, queens and rooks repeatedly circling each other without much changing.It was Erigaisi who found the breakthrough late, working his queen and bishop into Leko's position and setting up a decisive rook sacrifice, trading his rook for Leko's on h2, before his queen swept in with checks that left White's king with nowhere to hide.Leko resigned soon after.That win, alongside draws from Praggnanandhaa and Nihal Sarin, was enough to salvage a 2-2 draw against Hungary, even after Gukesh, who was on an unbeaten streak before the final round, lost to Hungary's in-form Gleb Dudin on the fourth board.The result left India on 18 points, level with Germany, but India's superior tiebreak score (405.5 Germany's 386.5) proved decisive, handing them silver behind a rampant Uzbekistan side that finished on 20.India bag Gaprindashvili CupThere was one more prize India walked away with, and it might be the most telling of all. The Gaprindashvili Cup, awarded to the federation with the best combined finish across the open and women's sections, went to India, their rank sum of 5 (silver in the open, bronze in women's) edging out Uzbekistan's 8 and the United States' 12. It capped a fortnight in which India's two teams, across ten days of chess, ended up the most consistent nation in Samarkand.Individual medals:Women: Savitha Shri (gold on Board 5), Divya Deshmukh (silver on Board 3), Koneru Humpy (bronze on Board 1), Vantika Agrawal (bronze on Board 4)Open: D Gukesh (silver on Board 4), R Praggnanandhaa (bronze on Board 1)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Justin Fields could be returning to New York
articles.summary: Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York.
articles.body:
Woody Johnson's favorite quarterback could be returning to New York .

Justin Fields , who was traded by the Jets to the Chiefs as part of the plan to have a capable replacement in the event Patrick Mahomes wasn't ready for Week 1, has emerged as an option for the Giants, who have made it clear they will look at all options.

Fields has been mentioned multiple times in recent days by multiple reporters, which means that the word is out that Fields could be a possibility for the Giants.

The Giants are expected to make a move as soon as Monday. Jameis Winston 's performance against the Titans on Sunday will surely be a factor in the question of whether they're looking for someone to serve as Winston's backup — or someone who could eventually supplant him while starter Jaxson Dart misses at least the balance of the regular season after knee surgery.

The two-year, $40 million contract Fields signed last year with the Jets included $10 million guaranteed for 2026. The Chiefs are paying him $3 million , and the Jets are paying $7 million. With Mahomes looking like Mahomes again, the Chiefs could recoup their 2027 sixth-round pick and unload the balance of Fields's 2026 salary.

The Chiefs also would have to be willing to elevate rookie Garrett Nussmeier into the QB2 role behind Mahomes, unless coach Andy Reid and G.M. Brett Veach have someone else in mind who could be the backup to Mahomes.

Giants coach John Harbaugh has limited experience against Fields. In 2021, Fields (then a rookie with the Bears), started a Week 11 game against the Ravens. He left with a rib injury after completing four of 11 passes for 79 yards and rushing one time for four yards. During his single season with the Steelers , Fields played three snaps in a Week 11 game against the Ravens that Russell Wilson started. Fields ran the ball twice for 17 yards. In the wild-card game that same year between the Steelers and Ravens, Fields played two snaps, throwing one pass that did not connect.

Still, Fields apparently is on the radar screen for a return to New York, where the other team that plays in MetLife Stadium will be paying him a lot more than whatever the Giants would contribute to his 2026 W-2.

articles.title: "I'm over the moon!" - Paris Brunner shines on U21 debut
articles.summary: Paris Brunner could hardly have wished for a better Germany U21 debut.The AS Monaco forward scored twice in Germany's 4-0 victory over Latvia, opening the sc...
articles.body:
Paris Brunner could hardly have wished for a better Germany U21 debut.

The AS Monaco forward scored twice in Germany's 4-0 victory over Latvia, opening the scoring after just 53 seconds before adding his second shortly before half-time.

"What a start!" Brunner said after the game. "I'm over the moon – first game for the U21s and then straight away a brace. The main thing is that we won. The brace is the icing on the cake."

The 20-year-old had only recently received his first U21 call-up, but coach Antonio Di Salvo was already impressed with what he saw.

"We don't want to slow him down," Di Salvo said, according to the report. The Germany coach believes Brunner's confidence and attacking qualities can make him an important player for the U21s.

Brunner himself was keen to keep the focus on the team rather than his personal achievement, adding that Germany had "played a really good game" and deserved the victory.

The result leaves Germany top of their qualifying group with 21 points from eight matches , while Brunner has immediately put his name forward for another start in the upcoming qualifiers.

articles.title: Zoff: ‘Mancini’s advantage is Italy cannot get any worse’
articles.summary: Dino Zoff was not encouraged by what he saw at the Stadio Olimpico on Friday evening, but the 1982 World Cup-winning captain believes there is only one direc...
articles.body:
Dino Zoff was not encouraged by what he saw at the Stadio Olimpico on Friday evening , but the 1982 World Cup-winning captain believes there is only one direction available to Roberto Mancini's Italy .

Speaking to La Repubblica after Friday's 2-0 defeat to Belgium , with quotes via CalcioMercato , Zoff pointed to the nerves that gripped the side early on. "It seemed very fearful to me initially. In the first half it suffered a lot," he said. "Afterwards it fought, but that tension I saw at the start struck me."

29 May 2000: Portrait of Dino Zoff of Italy during the Italian national team squad training held at the National Team Headquarters, in Coverciano, Florence, Italy. Mandatory Credit: Claudio Villa /Allsport

With three Nations League fixtures still to come in ten days, starting away to Vincenzo Montella's Turkiye, Zoff sees value in the schedule itself.

"You need to talk little and work a lot. These other three games will be important, the players will be able to spend time together. We are at the start of a new path and, even if there is not much time, I am fairly confident."

He was unbothered by the average age of Mancini's starting XI, which came in at 23. "Lads who are good can play at 16, in my opinion. The problems are elsewhere."

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 25: Alessandro Romano of Italy compete for the ball with Brandon Mechele during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and Belgium at Stadio Olimpico on September 25, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi/Getty Images)

Asked where those problems lie, the former goalkeeper pointed forward. "I would say up front, that is where it struggled. Even when we came out in the second half we did not score. You have to look for quality."

And while he accepts the job is harder than it was in 2018, that is precisely what gives him hope.

"Yes, it is obvious. We are coming off a dark period. It is also true that it cannot be done any worse than this. That works in his favour: it is easier to grow. In the situation we are in, we can only improve."

articles.title: Storylines to watch between the Vikings and Bucs in Week 3
articles.summary: The Vikings are looking to improve to 3-0 with a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings picked up two hard-earned wins in-division to begin the season. They head to Tampa Bay to face the winless Buccaneers on Sunday, rekindling an old-school NFC Central rivalry.

Can the Vikings avoid a letdown after a physical Week 2 game against the Bears ? Minnesota has a chance to create some space between itself and the rest of the NFC North. The Packers got humiliated on Thursday night, falling to 1-2. Chicago faces the Eagles on Monday night with Case Keenum starting at quarterback. The Lions play the Jets, who have proven, if nothing else, to be a tougher matchup than in years past.

Of course, what the other teams do won't matter if the Vikings keep winning. Here are the main storylines heading into Minnesota's Week 3 matchup against Tampa Bay.

Storylines to watch between the Vikings and Bucs in Week 3

The Vikings have gone 2-0 to begin the season despite the absence of Murray, who exited their Week 1 game against the Packers after three offensive drives. He cleared the concussion protocol on Monday, giving him a full week of practice ahead of this Sunday's game.

Murray told reporters on Thursday that he never felt he got into the flow of the season opener. Will he be able to protect the football? Minnesota hasn't turned the ball over since Murray threw an interception on his first pass as a Viking. The balance between opening up the offense with Murray's skill set and protecting the ball will be intriguing.

Minnesota has leaned on its rushing attack over its past seven games dating back to last season. But injuries have affected the running back room over the past two weeks, with Jordan Mason going on short-term injured reserve last week and Aaron Jones missing Wednesday's practice with a knee injury he sustained in Chicago.

Jones wasn't on the Vikings' final injury report on Friday, but how many touches will he get against the Buccaneers? He carried the ball 23 times for 105 yards against the Bears, his most carries in three seasons in Minnesota. But can he sustain that kind of workload while dealing with the knee injury? Or will the Vikings need to lean on DeeJay Dallas, Demond Claiborne, and potentially Jerome Ford to ease Jones' load?

Sunday's game couldn't look much different than last week for the Vikings. After a sloppy, rainy day at Soldier Field in Week 2, they will play under sunny skies with mid-80s temperatures, with the heat index potentially reaching 90 degrees.

The Buccaneers announced Friday that they will wear their white uniforms , meaning Minnesota will wear its purple home uniforms. Will the Vikings be able to handle the Florida heat after dealing with the fall-like Minnesota weather?

articles.title: Caleb Williams injury: Bears QB has Grade 2 hamstring strain, out 3-4 weeks
articles.summary: Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and will miss 3-4 weeks for the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Update 9/27 : Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and is expected to miss 3-4 weeks, according to ESPN . He is out for Chicago's Monday Night game against the Philadelphia Eagles , and is slated to miss the following two games against the New York Jets and Green Bay Packers . The Bears face the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6, then play on Thursday Night Football in Week 7 against the New England Patriots — two possible options for Williams' return. Chicago's backup QB Tyson Bagent has been in concussion protocol. Either Bagent or Case Keenum will start for the Bears in Week 3 against the Eagles.

Update Monday afternoon : Williams "avoided any major injury to his hamstring," according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero . He hasn't been ruled out for Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night yet. This seems like the best case scenario for the Bears. Ben Johnson called the injury "week to week."

Update : Williams will have an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of his hamstring injury, per Adam Schefter .

Caleb Williams looked like a potential MVP candidate during Week 1, as he led a Chicago Bears offense that hung 59 points on the board against the Carolina Panthers .

But the combination of weather in Chicago — and a Brian Flores-led Minnesota Vikings defense — has made for tougher sledding in Week 2.

And now the Bears quarterback could be dealing with a lower-body injury.

Williams had to be helped off the field after a short run midway through the fourth quarter, and the injury brought backup quarterback Tyson Bagent into the game.

You can see the moment here, as it appears Williams goes down with a non-contact injury:

The only sound you could hear after the play was Williams crying out in pain, as the Bears-heavy crowd at Soldier Field was stunned into silence. Williams as helped off the field, as Bagent entered the game.

Making matters worse, Chicago's possession stalled and a potential game-tying field goal was blocked, just as Williams was being taken to the locker room on a cart:

Now we wait on word regarding Chicago's star quarterback.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Stewart has 'concerns' over Scotland system
articles.summary: Michael Stewart fears the system Scotland are playing under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli will not best showcase the squad's talent.  An improved second...
articles.body:
Michael Stewart fears the system Scotland are playing under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli will not best showcase the squad's talent.

An improved second-half performance in Slovenia almost brought victory for Scotland in Saturday's Nations League opener but they ultimately had to settle for a 0-0 draw.

"One concern I would have moving forward when a manager is ideologically stuck to a system prior to actually dealing with a team or a group of players," Stewart told BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound.

"I've just got a bit of a concern as to seeing how you fit the likes of Ben Gannon-Doak or Josh McPake, who's been outstanding so far - how do they fit into this system? Scott McTominay's obviously got to come back as well.

"Where do you get those guys into the team as well because, for all the good play and opportunities that we created late on, a lot of that came when Ben Gannon-Doak came on high up on the right-hand side.

"You're trying to get your best players on to the park, irrespective of what the system. I'm just a little bit concerned that we're not going to be able to get our best players on the park in the areas of the pitch that are going to cause problems for the opposition."

Stewart regarded Saturday's result as "two points dropped" for the Scots, who played three at the back, wing-backs either side of two central midfielders and three players high up the pitch.

And Stewart praised the performance of "absolute gem" Billy Gilmour.

"He needs to be if not the first name on the sheet then certainly one of them and you need to build round him," Stewart said.

"You need to get him in positions where he can get on the ball, feed the likes of John McGinn, Scott McTominay, Josh McPake, Ben Gannon-Doak, Robbie Ure, Kieron Bowie.

"He's got to be the fulcrum of the side. He's the one that has that genuine top-class ability. You need to get him on the ball in the centre of the park."

articles.title: Cowboys interested in trade for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Cowboys are back in some trade rumors
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys see their window of opportunity to make a Super Bowl run as right now. Owner and general manager Jerry Jones hasn't been shy about making a move to improve his team, and he may already be laying the groundwork for a potential in-season trade.

NFL Insider Adam Schefter says the Cowboys, along with a handful of other teams, have inquired about trading for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Schefter also says that the Steelers are willing to listen to offers, but wouldn't deal their cornerback unless they got a strong compensation package in return.

The Cowboys front office hasn't been shy about making deals with the Steelers. They traded for George Pickens last year and acquired Broderick Jones before this season started. The team is also becoming very thin in the secondary with Cobie Durant out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury and P.J. Locke going on injured reserve.

Dallas also wants to give Christian Parker every tool he can for success, so a move for Porter Jr. would give him a prototypical, high-ceiling cornerback who could fit the scheme.

If Dallas is serious about going after a player like Porter Jr., it will truly be an all-in move with their sights set on a championship run.

articles.title: Linda Cohn calls out Stephanie White as Caitlin Clark’s sideline exchange fuels playoff scrutiny
articles.summary: Linda Cohn criticized Stephanie White after Caitlin Clark’s sideline exchange with assistant coach Briann January drew attention. As Indiana prepares for the...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark helped Indiana beat the WNBA's top seed, but a brief sideline exchange became a separate story. Now Linda Cohn is questioning Stephanie White's leadership, putting the Fever's coaching staff under scrutiny before the playoffs.

The former ESPN anchor criticized White after cameras captured assistant coach Briann January speaking animatedly to Clark during Tuesday's victory over Minnesota . Cohn argued that a head coach must take responsibility for how assistants address players.

Her comments followed Thursday's lopsided loss to the same opponent, a turnaround that made Indiana's final regular-season week especially jarring. Cohn suggested the earlier interaction could have carried consequences beyond the moment captured on the broadcast.

Indiana's week had already begun with a 93-77 loss to Washington on Sunday. The uneven finish supplied plenty to examine on the court before Cohn's comments shifted additional attention toward communication on the Fever's coaching staff.

Cohn's strongest criticism focused on public communication. She questioned why January would address Clark that way within view of spectators, arguing that the setting mattered even if the guard had been playing poorly during the game.

"Stephanie White, this ultimately falls on you," Cohn said in comments reported by EssentiallySports. Her argument placed responsibility with the head coach, extending the discussion beyond January's conduct to the standards White sets for her staff.

Cohn also urged the Fever to handle such matters during practice or a timeout. Her criticism was a judgment about coaching approach, however, rather than evidence that she knew the substance of the conversation between January and Clark.

The clip leaves important questions unanswered

According to reporting carried by AOL, January appeared animated and pointed toward Clark during their interaction. Clark listened briefly, responded and walked away. The broadcast did not clearly capture their words, leaving the actual conversation unresolved.

Some viewers interpreted January's opening words as "stay away from me," but that reading has not been confirmed. Without clear audio, presenting a social media interpretation as a verified quotation would give the footage more certainty than it supports.

Cohn acknowledged that limitation herself, saying she did not know what January said. That admission is central to assessing her criticism: She objected to the apparent public confrontation while conceding that its subject and context remained unclear.

The exchange happened during Indiana's 96-77 victory over Minnesota on Sept. 22. Clark finished with 27 points, 9 assists and 7 rebounds, putting together a productive all-around performance as the Fever completed their regular-season home schedule.

Indiana's defense helped create the separation. The Fever led 31-16 after the opening quarter and 57-34 at halftime, according to the team's recap. Minnesota committed 17 turnovers, which Indiana converted into 21 points during the win.

The game also required a response under pressure. Minnesota cut the deficit to 7 points before Indiana regained control. That sequence offered a basketball explanation for the evening's intensity, though it does not explain the sideline conversation.

Minnesota's response changed the playoff picture

Thursday's rematch brought a much different result. Minnesota won 86-66 on Sept. 24, sending Indiana into the playoffs as the No. 6 seed. The Associated Press reported that Kayla McBride led the Lynx with 22 points.

McBride made 6 of 10 attempts from 3-point range, while Clark managed a season-low 2 points on 1-for-12 shooting. Indiana fell behind 25-4 late in the opening quarter, creating a deficit it never successfully overcame that night.

Those details show how thoroughly the game turned against Indiana. They do not establish Cohn's suggested cause. A poor shooting night and an early defensive breakdown can be documented; their connection to Tuesday's exchange has not been demonstrated.

White's assessment adds a different perspective

White's comments after Tuesday's victory emphasized resilience. In the Fever's published recap, she praised her players for staying together and responding to her challenge after allowing Minnesota back into the game, while acknowledging their recurring lapses in concentration.

That account complicates the suggestion that the evening already showed a team unraveling. White described a group that recovered from trouble together. Her assessment does not settle questions about January, but it belongs alongside criticism of the footage.

Clark also expressed confidence in Indiana's locker room after the victory and identified consistency as the next step. Her public assessment centered on sustaining the team's best basketball, providing useful context beyond an isolated, widely discussed sideline interaction.

January brings championship experience to the bench

January's connection to the Fever stretches well beyond this coaching assignment. Indiana drafted her in 2009, and she helped the franchise win the 2012 WNBA championship. She later returned to work on White's staff as an assistant coach.

Her playing résumé includes an All-Star selection in 2014 and 7 WNBA All-Defensive team selections. Those accomplishments establish substantial experience at this level, even as viewers debate whether her approach during this particular interaction with Clark was appropriate.

One fun fact: January's athletic background extends beyond basketball. Her official WNBA biography says she holds a black belt in karate and won a state high jump title in 2004 while attending high school in Spokane, Washington.

Clark has challenged the narratives around her

The broader discussion followed Clark's public questioning of how stories about her develop. In a July interview, she said coverage was "not always based in reality," addressing the gap she saw between outside narratives and her own experience.

That earlier remark should not be treated as a direct response to this week's exchange. It does, however, provide relevant background when assessing claims about her relationships with coaches, particularly claims built primarily around gestures and facial expressions.

Cohn brings her own long broadcasting history to the discussion. ESPN announced her retirement effective June 30 after a career that began at the network in 1992. Describing her as a former ESPN anchor is therefore accurate here.

Indiana's next test comes against Las Vegas

Indiana's first-round opponent is the Las Vegas Aces , according to reporting following Thursday's finale. That matchup gives White and her players a concrete priority after a week that produced both an encouraging victory and a difficult closing performance.

For the Fever, the clearest basketball questions involve their starts, defensive execution and ability to sustain productive stretches. The final games supplied examples of those challenges without requiring assumptions about what players or coaches privately think of one another.

Cohn has made her position clear: White should answer for how her staff communicates publicly. Whether that criticism identifies a deeper problem remains unresolved. Indiana's playoff response will provide fresh evidence about its basketball, rather than a transcript of Tuesday.

Fun fact: On July 6, 2024, Caitlin Clark became the first WNBA rookie to record a triple-double, finishing with 19 points, 13 assists and 12 rebounds in Indiana's 83-78 victory over New York.

Cohn criticized White's oversight of the Fever's public sideline communication. She placed full responsibility on the head coach.

January's exact words to Clark remain unverified. The broadcast did not clearly capture the brief conversation.

Indiana split its final Minnesota matchups and will face Las Vegas.

No established evidence links the exchange to Thursday's defeat.

articles.title: Henry, Ferguson and turnovers: Four keys to Ravens-Cowboys
articles.summary: The Ravens' trip to Brazil features star power on both sidelines, but a handful of critical details could determine if they earn a victory.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys have plenty of marquee names . Lamar Jackson , Derrick Henry , Dak Prescott , CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , and Kyle Hamilton all qualify. All are more than capable of producing the highlight-reel moments that dominate postgame discussions. Games between talented teams, however, often hinge on smaller details that receive far less attention . Red-zone execution, ball security, discipline, and the ability to lean into a favorable matchup can matter as much as any spectacular play.

As the Ravens prepare for a unique Week 3 matchup in Brazil, plenty of room exists for tense moments. Still, don't be shocked if these four factors could ultimately determine the outcome.

Take Jake Ferguson away from Dak Prescott in the red zone

It doesn't get much better than Jake Ferguson's Week 2 stat line. Four targets... Four receptions... 43 yards receiving... Two touchdown receptions. The only thing missing is the bomb from Prescott, but they don't need it.

Known as a primary red-zone and goal-line weapon for Dak Prescott, over 80% of Ferguson's career scores come from inside the 20-yard line (including seven of eight in 2025). If Baltimore can force Prescott to look elsewhere, he'll still have options, namely CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but at least this removes one threat.

The Ravens don't necessarily have to eliminate Ferguson from the game entirely. They just need to make life harder when the field shrinks. If Dallas settles for field goals instead of touchdowns on a few possessions, Baltimore's defense will have done its job.

Sometimes, you have to ride your superstars and live with the consequences, be they good or bad. The Cowboys have surrendered 173.5 rushing yards per contest. Only three NFL teams have been worse through two games. The Ravens employ the great Derrick Henry.

This isn't difficult. No one's familiar with the playing surface at Maracanã Stadium. The game plan should seem simple. Win or lose this one by leaning on the future Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee.

Establishing Henry early could also create opportunities elsewhere. A successful ground attack would help control time of possession, open throwing lanes for Lamar Jackson, and potentially wear down a defense that has struggled to stop opposing rushing attacks.

Ravens must stop beating themselves with penalties

This portion of the story almost writes itself. The Ravens have committed 17 penalties through two games. Those infractions have resulted in 120 yards. Seriously, what else needs to be said? Winning in the NFL is hard enough. Winning becomes nearly impossible when a team short-circuits its own efforts.

Baltimore has already seen explosive plays erased and promising drives stalled because of self-inflicted mistakes. Against an opponent as talented as Dallas, giving away free yardage is a dangerous game to play.

If there's one thing that the Cowboys defense does well, it's ripping the football out. Over two games, the Cowboys have forced seven fumbles and recovered two. Baltimore lost a fumble in Week 1 and threw an interception in Week 2. Protecting the ball will be key in a game where every yard, stop, and mistake will matter more than usual.

Turnovers can change games in an instant. A promising drive can disappear. Momentum can shift. A close contest can suddenly become an uphill battle. The Ravens don't need to play perfectly, but they do need to avoid giving Dallas extra possessions.

Baltimore's formula isn't particularly complicated. Feed Derrick Henry, tighten up the discipline issues, make Prescott work harder in the red zone, and secure the football. None of those tasks will guarantee victory, but together they provide a blueprint for success.

The Ravens and Cowboys possess enough star power to produce fireworks at any moment. When the final whistle sounds in Brazil, though, the difference may come down to which team handled the fundamentals better. In a matchup that feels evenly balanced on paper, those details could decide everything.

articles.title: Liverpool star takes aim at Jurgen Klopp’s Germany side
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo Criticises Germany as Jurgen Klopp’s Return Ends in Heated Netherlands DrawJurgen Klopp’s return to the touchline brought a familiar sight, old Li...
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo Criticises Germany as Jurgen Klopp's Return Ends in Heated Netherlands Draw

Jurgen Klopp's return to the touchline brought a familiar sight, old Liverpool faces, a good deal of noise, and one awkward moment that dominated the fallout. Germany drew with the Netherlands in the Nations League, but the bigger talking point was not the result. It was the decision to play on while Brian Brobbey was down injured.

Klopp came up against Virgil van Dijk , Ryan Gravenberch and Cody Gakpo, players he knows well from his Liverpool days. Pre-match sentiment was predictable enough. Once the game got going, sentiment disappeared. These fixtures rarely drift into polite territory and this one followed the same pattern.

The key flashpoint arrived shortly after the half-hour. Brobbey was on the ground and the Netherlands expected the ball to be put out of play. Germany carried on. Felix Nmecha finished the move and scored while the Dutch forward remained stricken.

The reaction from the Netherlands was immediate and, after the match, Gakpo made it plain where he stood. "In our opinion, that is unsportsmanlike," he said. "There is no rule for it, but I think it is normal to play the ball out of bounds when someone is lying on the ground. They decided not to do that; that was not sporting, which made things a bit more heated."

That is the issue in simple terms. There may be no law requiring a stoppage, but players still work off a code. When one side feels that code has been ignored, tempers go quickly.

Jurgen Klopp reunion with former Liverpool players

Before and after the match, Klopp seemed relaxed enough. He greeted Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Gakpo individually and spent extra time with Van Dijk after full-time. That part looked genuine. On the pitch, none of it mattered.

Gakpo then had the final say where it counted, scoring the late equaliser that earned Xavi a point in his first match in charge of the Dutch side. It gave the celebrations extra edge, which was hardly surprising given what had gone before.

Nations League draw leaves familiar debate

There is no evidence this was a touchline instruction from Klopp. More likely, the players made the call in real time and accepted the consequences. Even so, the argument around sportsmanship is not going anywhere. Modern football is full of these moments, players pushing every limit, waiting for referees to intervene rather than doing the obvious thing themselves.

This match finished level, but it did not feel calm. Germany got the goal, the Netherlands got the equaliser, and Gakpo made sure nobody ignored the incident that sat over the whole night.

articles.body:
Kevin Schade Transfer Latest as Manchester United Weigh Brentford Opportunity

Manchester United could be emerging as a club to watch in the developing Kevin Schade transfer story, with uncertainty continuing to surround the Brentford forward's future. According to Caught Offside , there is growing doubt over whether the Bundesliga-born Germany international will commit his long-term future to Brentford despite the club's efforts to secure fresh terms.

The latest information points to a situation that remains open rather than advanced. Brentford have been keen to reward Schade after what has been described as his "fine start to the season", but crucially, attempts to move discussions forward do not appear to have delivered a breakthrough. The key line in this update is that "initial contacts earlier in the season have not progressed anywhere meaningful."

Manchester United Tracking Kevin Schade Situation

For Manchester United, this is the type of market development that tends to attract close internal attention. Schade is still viewed as a player with significant upside, and if contractual talks remain stalled, the possibility of movement in a forthcoming window naturally grows. The report states that "Manchester United could about to get involved in the Kevin Schade transfer saga", a line that will inevitably spark interest among supporters looking at wide attacking reinforcements.

Brentford, for their part, are understood to be determined to keep hold of the player. Yet that stance does not remove the wider tension around his future. As noted in the source report, "Schade is likely to be one to watch in the winter window", which suggests rival clubs may begin positioning themselves if there is still no major progress on a new deal.

There is no suggestion that an exit is imminent, and Brentford's preference is clear. Still, contract situations can shape the direction of a transfer market very quickly, especially when a player is performing well and attracting outside admiration. In Schade's case, the current picture is one of cautious intrigue rather than certainty, but it is enough to place his name firmly on the winter shortlist conversation.

From a Manchester United fan perspective, this feels like one of those situations worth watching closely rather than getting carried away with too early. Kevin Schade has qualities that would appeal, pace, directness, physicality and the sense that there is still more to come from him. If United are looking for attackers who can stretch games and offer something different in transition, then he fits part of that brief.

What stands out most is the contract angle. When a report says "initial contacts earlier in the season have not progressed anywhere meaningful", that is usually where opportunity starts for other clubs. United have to be smarter in these moments, identifying players before the price climbs too far or the queue becomes too long. Brentford are excellent sellers when they choose the right moment, so this would never be a straightforward deal.

Supporters would probably have mixed reactions because Schade is not yet a marquee name. That said, United need more than reputation. They need players who can improve the squad balance and raise the athletic level in the frontline. If "Schade is likely to be one to watch in the winter window", then United should absolutely be doing their homework now. This feels like the kind of move that could make sense if the recruitment team truly believe his ceiling is high enough.

articles.title: Three EDGE Prospects that could fit in well with the Chicago Bears
articles.summary: Bears could use their first round selection on an edge rusher, and likely they'll be picking somewhere in the middle, or later portion of the round
articles.body:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, it was very clear what the top position of need was for the Chicago Bears - edge rusher. Then came the season opener, when Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young , who has been the definition of "mid" through the first three years of his career, shredded them for 361 yards passing.

While they have gotten home to the opposing quarterback, racking up five sacks through the first two games, it is only a middle-of-the-pack showing. Montez Sweat is obviously, with apologies to Evander Holyfield, "the real deal." He's a tour de force, but he needs help.

The Bears could very easily use their first round selection on an edge rusher, and most likely, they'll be picking somewhere in the middle, or later portion of the round.

Here are three edge rushers who might be available when they're on the board.

A five-star recruit who was ranked #2 in the state of Alabama and #28 nationally, he was as blue chip as it gets coming out og high school in 2023.

Given how deep Bama's front is, he didn't get his chance until last year, after redshirting in 2024. He racked up nine sacks and 45 pressures last term, adding 34 run stoppagess and three forced fumbles. And in the words of Frank Sinatra, "the best is yet to come."

If you're going for an upside/potential kind of pick, then this is absolutely the way to go. At SEC Media Day, Arkansas head coach Ryan Silverfield discussed the upside of Rhodes , as well as just how far he's come thus far. He noted the weight he put on.

"His body has already changed in the short time with our new strength and conditioning staff," Silverfield said.

"We're seeing him take steps in the right direction in a leadership role. We're going to continue to push him." An all-SEC second team selection last season, this year he could easily develop into first team, and then, maybe who knows, All-American?

He's been a top rated prospect for awhile now, so there is certainly a lot of good tape available on him. To employ the very over-used buzz-phrase, he truly "sets the edge." One could say he even makes sure that no one "breaks outside contain."

But seriously folks, Uiagalelei brings the pressure even when he isn't racking up TFLs or sacks. He's an absolutle monster on passing downs, but still needs work on run downs.

He's got too many missed tackles on his CV, but if cleans that up, we're talking definite first round material.

articles.title: Forget anonymous critic, No. 1 Texas Longhorns have shown they're far from soft | Golden
articles.summary: One anonymous coach out there put a rise in the Texas Longhorns by calling the team soft. I don't see it. Soft teams don't win hard-fought games like Texas h...
articles.body:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. - Keep on questioning the Texas Longhorns .

Tell a journalist they can't win in tough environments?

In the moments after Saturday's 20-17 win over No. 14 Tennesse e before 109,915 fans at raucous Neyland Stadium, the No. 1-ranked Horns took aim at their haters, particularly one anonymous coach who questioned the team's toughness in an interview with The Athletic .

"They look the part. They're fast. They can bend but they don't have an edge to them. They're soft everywhere," that coach said.

Soft teams don't beat Ohio State and Tennessee in a span of three weeks. Soft teams don't lead all Power Four teams with 16 conference wins since 2023. Soft teams don't find a way to shut down one of the nation's most vaunted rushing attacks on the road on the same day they commit 11 penalties.

"I'm not sure who wrote the article today and what coach said we weren't a physical football team," Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian said. "(They) may want to write another article."

With a much-needed bye week coming up, Texas is 4-0 for the second time in three seasons and while its offensive struggles are out there for all to see, the collective stood shoulder to shoulder to deliver their first road win over a ranked SEC opponent since they beat Texas A&M in College Station in 2024. They'll be a double-digit bet to spank Oklahoma in two weeks before a tough gantlet against resurgent Florida , high scoring Ole Miss and the comeback kids from Mississippi State .

The Longhorns are far from a finished product. But it would be a mistake to question their resolve. Sure, they haven't been as explosive despite spending a football's Fort Knox on some high-priced transfers.

Yeah, that offensive line resembled five 300-pound blocks of Swiss cheese as quarterback Arch Manning ran for his life in Knoxville. And yes, they commit more penalties at times than an insider trader before The Bell.

Somehow, the officials allowed an onside kick that looked more like a drop kick. That led to Texas' defense having to defend a Hail Mary pass into the end zone that never should have happened, according to former NFL referee Terry McAulay , who's now a rules analyst on NBC.

But the Longhorns are tough. Proven. Resilient.

Texas offensive line had protection struggles

Manning, who has taken a beaten in some social media circles, took a physical pounding in the Scruffy City as he was on the receiving end of six sacks. Undaunted, Texas' QB1 stood tall and still completed 14 of 19 passes on a day when he could have used some of President Trump's security detail up front. The Volunteers took big shots at him when he decided to bail out of the pocket, but Manning never buckled under the pressure.

Those bruises will heal soon enough and by the time the Longhorns take the field against Oklahoma in Dallas, they'll still be atop the national rankings.

Two weeks after they climbed out of a Royal-Memorial Stadium grave by scoring 21 fourth-quarter points to hand Ohio State its first loss , the Horns opened SEC play Saturday with a grind-it-out, well-earned win in one of the league's most hostile road environments. They showed more mettle than a coal miner who had just requested more overtime after a 60-hour work week.

When a team can send more than 109,000 fans and the sitting U.S. president home disappointed in the final result - Trump had picked the Volunteers to win, received two loud ovations when he appeared on the Neyland Stadium scoreboard and still went home with an L - it's a testament to what's swimming around in its gut.

Texas felt challenged and rose to the moment

Texas defensive tackle Hero Kanu is one of the most likable players on this roster, but he didn't go all Mayberry RFD when the question of Texas' toughness, or a perceived lack thereof, came up after the game.

"We were challenged," Kanu said. "They told us we weren't physical or something like that. We had to show them. I don't know how many rushing yards they had, but it was definitely not 298."

Kanu was referring to the vaunted Tennessee run game, which came in averaging 298.67 yards, which ranked fourth in the country. Texas held the Volunteers to 228 yards under that average while edge rusher Colin Simmons unleashed a sacks tirade with a school record-tying five. Simmons went from two sacks in the first three games to leading the country with seven before the night games started.

MORE COLLEGE FOOTBALL : Reeling Aggies lose at LSU

It didn't come without controversy. Simmons celebrated his second sack in the second quarter by simulating taking a bathroom break on the finely manicured grass near the end zone, turning what would been a fourth-and-29 situation into a momentum-changing first down that woke up the Volunteers.

In the interview room, Simmons thanked God, apologized and chalked up his actions to the emotion of the moment.

There has to be a measure of comfort for a struggling offense in knowing if it can produce a couple of touchdowns and a couple of field goals, there's still a chance that he defense will hold it down for the win.

"If they can get us 20 points, there's no reason for us losing," Kanu said. "Our defense is going to step up on days like this."

This is a team with issues that need fixing. It's a work in progress that retains a nice bit of upside as it gets ready for the reeling Sooners followed by five consecutive games against ranked teams.

The Horns don't always look like world beaters, but they show up for the fight.

articles.title: Giants' John Harbaugh, Matt Nagy must navigate around the negatives
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy didn't anticipate injuries to change their 2026 NFL season but they'll need to adjust.
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy will want to forget the abysmal outing their team had at SoFi Bank Stadium this past Monday. The untimely season-ending injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart , the lack of morale amongst the core unit, and an offensive output that has them wondering how to move forward with their strategy into Week 3.

Nagy's offense was horrid on third-down conversion attempts and produced a rate of just 21 percent through 14 attempts. Hope was quickly lost in the 28-6 obliteration at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams . Perhaps it was the devastation of watching Dart leave the field in such anguish rather than the team's true inability to compete.

Nevertheless, the Rams thrived substantially while Nagy's offense continued to yield total nothingness outside the power leg of punter Jordan Stout and six yielded points from kicker Dominic Zvada.

Nagy may be forced to navigate away from his propensity to use 21-personnel given the limitations of reserve quarterback James Winston. Giants fans can expect to see fewer designed quarterback running plays, but Nagy shouldn't totally negate the power running game simply because Dart isn't in the lineup.

Nagy's entire playbook is built around precision, and the pressure of the Rams crowd might've rattled his offensive personnel in the primetime lights.

But the talent on the Giants roster still should allow them to prosper in an NFC East division where none of their competitors present true defensive dominance. For Nagy, he's proved that he has the ability to adjust on the fly, but time will tell what sort of adjustments he will make to propel the Giants throughout the 2026 NFL season.

articles.summary: Teófilo Gutiérrez confesó la lesión con la que jugó durante años y la fecha de su cirugía Por qué funciona: Las citas te
articles.body: A pocos meses de su retiro profesional del fútbol a los 41 años, Teófilo Gutiérrez pasó por los micrófonos de la revista Semana para repasar su prolífica y polémica trayectoria. Entre sus confesiones, el delantero barranquillero dio a conocer un detalle médico inédito: ha competido durante años con una fractura en el rostro que no ha podido corregir mediante cirugía por sus compromisos deportivos. Durante la entrevista, 'Teo' fue interrogado sobre los golpes físicos más duros de su carrera y reveló que sufre una fractura en el tabique nasal, producto de un cruce en cancha con el mediocampista Baldomero Perlaza. "Más de una vez me dejaron un recuerdo... el tabique me lo fracturó un poco", confesó el delantero, explicando por qué nunca entró al quirófano para solucionar el problema: "No me he podido operar. Siempre en Junior es 'no, mañana, pasado, que después, no hay tiempo'. En Junior he estado [ganando] títulos, [jugando] partidos". El jugador calificó la revelación como un secreto que ilustra los sacrificios invisibles de la alta competencia: "Es lo que deja el fútbol y mucha gente no sabe". Además de su estado físico, el exfutbolista de la Selección Colombia abordó varios momentos trascendentales de su carrera: Con títulos en Junior de Barranquilla, Deportivo Cali, River Plate y una distinción como Rey de América, Teófilo Gutiérrez dejará los terrenos de juego tras programar su 'Last Dance' de despedida, momento en el que finalmente podrá someterse a la intervención quirúrgica pendiente.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 8: Athletics leads India’s seven-medal haul, three boxers assure medals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed another productive day at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, adding seven medals on Sunday as athletics emerged as the biggest
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed another productive day at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, adding seven medals on Sunday as athletics emerged as the biggest contributor with five podium finishes, while squash delivered two silver medals.The medal haul included silver medals for Ancy Sojan and Sarvesh Kushare, bronze medals for Parul Chaudhary, Tejaswin Shankar and Harita Bhadra, and two silver medals in squash through Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh.India's boxing campaign also received a major boost, with Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal and Narender Berwal all assuring themselves of medals by reaching the semifinals in their respective categories.There was disappointment in badminton, however, as PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda, Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Tanisha Crasto-Dhruv Kapila all bowed out in the quarterfinals of their individual events.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAthletics produces five-medal haulAthletics provided India with its biggest haul of the day.Parul Chaudhary produced one of the standout performances, breaking her personal best and setting a new national record of 9:08.67 to win bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase. It was Parul's second Asian Games steeplechase medal after she won silver in the same event at Hangzhou in 2022.Bahrain's Winfred Yavi won gold in 9:04.36, while Kazakhstan's Norah Jeruto Tanui took silver in 9:06.82. India's Ankita also set a personal best of 9:19.24 but finished fourth.Ancy Sojan came agonisingly close to gold in the women's long jump. Her 6.53m effort in the fifth round put her in front, but China's Huang Yingying produced a 6.55m jump with her final attempt to snatch the title by two centimetres.Shaili Singh was also denied a medal in the final round. Her 6.42m had put her third, but China's Mengyi Tan jumped 6.46m with her final attempt to move into bronze-medal position.In the men's high jump, Sarvesh Kushare also had to settle for silver after a closely fought contest. He cleared 2.25m on his second attempt, but Chinese Taipei's Chao Hsuan-Fu had already cleared the height on his first attempt.Tejaswin Shankar completed India's athletics medal haul with bronze in the decathlon. After two gruelling days, Tejaswin won the final event, the 1500m, in 4:33.09 and finished with 7,934 points. Japan's Yuma Maruyama won gold with 8,123 points, while China's Xinghua Chen took silver.Earlier, Harita Bhadra won bronze in the women's 200m, clocking 23.20 seconds to edge Japan's Ido Abigeirufuka by 0.01 seconds. Singapore's Shanti Pereira won gold in 22.78s and China's Chen Yujie took silver in 22.93s.Anahat, Abhay win squash silverIndia's wait for a squash singles gold at the Asian Games continued, but both Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh produced historic silver-medal finishes.World No. 5 Sivasangari Subramaniam defeated 18-year-old Anahat 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 in the women's singles final, while world No. 17 Ng Eain Yow beat Abhay 11-9, 11-5, 11-5 in the men's final.Malaysia therefore swept both singles gold medals.For Anahat, the silver was nevertheless a landmark achievement as she became the first Indian woman to reach an Asian Games squash singles final. The singles results also ended India's hopes of taking the direct qualification opportunity for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics through the Asian Games individual competition.Three boxers assure medalsWhile squash narrowly missed out on gold, Indian boxing delivered three guaranteed medals.Parveen Hooda defeated Uzbekistan's world championships silver medallist Navbakhor Khamidova 5-0 in the women's 65kg quarterfinal to reach the semifinals.It was Parveen's first bout of the Games after receiving a walkover in the previous round. She said she was beginning to regain confidence after returning from a suspension and moving up from 57kg to 65kg.Ankush Panghal also advanced with a dominant 5-0 win over Tajikistan's Nekruz Salimov in the men's 80kg quarterfinal. The Commonwealth Games gold medallist controlled the contest from the opening round and secured his Asian Games debut medal.Narender Berwal completed the trio of assured medals by stopping Thailand's Adthapong Saengtep in the men's 90+kg quarterfinal in less than two minutes. The Indian landed a barrage of heavy blows and forced three standing counts before the referee stopped the contest.The day ended in disappointment for Sachin Siwach, however, as the Commonwealth Games champion lost 0-5 to Japan's Shunsuke Kitamoto in the men's 60kg quarterfinal.Badminton suffers quarterfinal exitsBadminton provided one of India's biggest disappointments on Sunday.PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda, Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Tanisha Crasto-Dhruv Kapila all lost their respective quarterfinals, meaning India failed to win an individual badminton medal at the Games.Two-time Olympic medallist Sindhu, playing her third match in less than 24 hours, went down 21-11, 18-21, 10-21 to Tokyo Olympic champion Chen Yu Fei."It's a bit hurtful but I need to recover from this. It would have been good if I would have gone to the semifinals. Unfortunate but never mind, these things keep happening. It's important to get back stronger," Sindhu said.Unnati, 19, fought hard before losing 16-21, 21-14, 17-21 to three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi.Treesa and Gayatri, who won a maiden World Championships bronze last month, lost 18-21, 9-21 to Malaysia's Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan. Tanisha and Dhruv also pushed world No. 1 Chinese pair Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dongping before losing 14-21, 21-18, 18-21.India had won three badminton medals at Hangzhou, including men's doubles gold through Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, but none of the individual competitors could reach the semifinals this time.More action across disciplinesIndia also recorded important wins elsewhere. The women's hockey side beat Singapore 7-0, while the men's volleyball side defeated Vietnam 3-0.Indian archers advanced in all six team events contested, including the men's and women's compound teams, compound mixed team, recurve men's and women's teams, and recurve mixed team.In athletics, Mohammed Afsal qualified for the men's 800m final, while India's women's 4x100m relay quartet of Abinaya Rajarajan, Tamanna, Sneha Sathyanarayana and Sudeshna Shivankar topped its heat to reach the final.India also progressed in surfing and continued its campaign in shooting, while there were mixed results in fencing, sepaktakraw, kurash and equestrian.With seven medals added on Sunday and three more assured in boxing, Day 8 provided India with plenty of positives even as the medal tally remained short of the gold-medal gains needed to climb the standings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
