articles.title: Sidney Crosby built a fortune beyond his NHL salary inside the Pittsburgh Penguins legend’s $100 million career, from contracts and endorsements to investments and luxury assets
articles.summary: Explore how Sidney Crosby built a fortune beyond his NHL salary through lucrative contracts, strategic endorsements, and investments, making him a financial powerhouse in the sports world.
articles.body: Sidney Crosby has played all his NHL career with the Pittsburgh Penguins, and his consistent on-ice contributions have created one of the biggest earning profiles in hockey. From his first entry-level contract to his subsequent long-term deals, his career contracts have totalled more than $150 million in total contract value. He is listed as making about $156.8 million in career contract earnings on current contract databases.The financial picture isn’t just his salary, either. Crosby has established long-term partnerships with major brands and has extended his entrepreneurial activities by becoming a shareholder and business partner at the Swiss watchmaker NORQAIN. That mix of NHL earnings, endorsement deals and business interests goes a long way toward explaining the size of the Penguins captain’s fortune.Sidney Crosby’s $150 million NHL career earnings reveal Penguins star’s lasting financial impactSidney Crosby was the first overall pick by the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2005 and became the face of the franchise right away. His contract history is today a major financial record, more than 20 years later. CapWages reports his career contract value at around $156.8 million, well above the $150 million plateau for NHL earnings.His largest single deal was a 12-year, $104.4 million contract signed in 2012. The deal was worth an average annual value of $8.7 million after his entry-level deal. Crosby then signed another two-year, $17.4 million extension in September 2024, maintaining the same $8.7 million annual average through the 2026-27 season.Sidney Crosby’s career earnings with Pittsburgh PenguinsCrosby’s NHL earnings have been spread across four major contracts and, in the later years of his career, his pay has been surprisingly consistent. His $8.7 million average annual value is notable because it ties into both his birth date (August 7) and his No. 87 jersey.NHL.com confirmed his most recent contract is worth $17.4 million over two years, starting with the 2025-26 season and ending in 2026-27. Crosby is in the final season of that deal now, and the next contract situation is a topic of conversation for September of 2026.ContractTermTotal valueAverage annual valueEntry-level contract2005-08$3.94 millionApproximately $1.31 millionSecond contract2008-12$43.5 million$8.7 millionLong-term contract2012-25$104.4 million$8.7 millionCurrent extension2025-27$17.4 million$8.7 millionReported career contract value—~$156.8 million—His current structure also demonstrates how NHL pay can be split between base salary and signing bonuses. Crosby is set to earn $9.78 million in 2025-26, including a $9 million signing bonus. The total for 2026-27 is $7.62 million, with a $6.53 million signing bonus.The numbers also put his career financial path in perspective. Most of Crosby’s public earnings have come from his playing career, but he’s been a big commercial force outside of the Pittsburgh Penguins for some time.Sidney Crosby’s contracts and endorsement portfolioCrosby’s commercial value grew almost as quickly as his reputation in the NHL. He started with endorsements for PepsiCo and Gatorade before entering long-term relationships with Tim Hortons and Reebok. Sportsnet called those relationships the foundation of Crosby’s marketing career.Reebok’s relationship with Crosby later carried on to Adidas after the German sportswear giant acquired Reebok. In 2015, Crosby signed a six-year endorsement deal with Adidas, and other long-time commercial partnerships have included Tim Hortons and Gatorade.The key difference is that Crosby's commercial portfolio has not been limited to traditional advertising. In April 2025, NORQAIN announced Crosby had become a shareholder and business partner in the independent Swiss watch company. The move gave him a direct ownership stake, not just another promotional deal.The partnership was further strengthened when NORQAIN became the official luxury sports watch partner of the NHL. NHL.com reported the league’s multiyear partnership with NORQAIN and said Crosby is a shareholder.The structure is yet another example of Crosby expanding his financial interests beyond the rink. Exact income from individual endorsement contracts is not released publicly across the entire portfolio, so figures for his annual off-ice income vary and should be viewed as estimates and not confirmed salary figures.Sidney Crosby’s investments and luxury assetsCrosby’s financial footprint also includes assets amassed over his long career, though the details of his full investment portfolio are not publicly known. Many private investments have not been officially disclosed in terms of their value and ownership structure, unlike his NHL contracts and NORQAIN shareholding.Crosby has publicly reported an asset profile in real estate. He purchased a house in the Pittsburgh area early in his career, and also owned property in Nova Scotia. However, valuation estimates for privately held residences tend to vary significantly today, so it can be difficult to make precise estimates without recent transaction records.His relationship with NORQAIN is better documented. The company officially names Crosby a shareholder and business partner, giving him a direct stake in the watchmaker’s business beyond a typical athlete endorsement.That uncertainty means his financial story is a work in progress, not a finished career balance sheet. Whatever comes of it from here, the most important thing is that Sidney Crosby has turned more than two decades with the Pittsburgh Penguins into a career contract worth over $150 million, and his endorsements and business interests have created additional streams of wealth outside of NHL salary.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is Gavin Bazunu, and why is he boycotting the Ireland vs Israel match?
articles.summary: Bazunu says his decision to withdraw was based on a ‘personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong’.
articles.body:
Footballer Gavin Bazunu is being hailed as a hero following his decision to withdraw from Ireland’s squad to face Israel in a UEFA Nations League match , which has been a point of contention between the Irish public and football officials since its confirmation in February.

Bazunu, who has been the Republic of Ireland’s first-choice goalkeeper in recent games, posted a statement on his social media accounts on Saturday, saying he felt “it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel”.

Subsequently, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) announced that the 24-year-old would be replaced in the squad for Sunday’s fixture , which will be the first of two games that Ireland will play against Israel in a period of eight days.

Bazunu’s public stance to opt out of the game has been hailed by football fans, former Irish footballers, politicians, and pro-Palestine activists.

Al Jazeera breaks down the background to his withdrawal, the reaction to it, and the FAI’s decisions leading up to the match:

The six-foot-two-inch (1.88m) goalkeeper is a Dublin-born footballer of Irish and Nigerian descent, who rose through the ranks of Ireland’s youth football system to become the country’s first-choice shot-stopper.

Nigerian on his father’s side, Bazunu was part of Ireland’s age-group teams from the under-15 level before making his senior team debut as a teenager in 2021.

Bazunu’s brilliance in goal was spotted by English Premier League giants Manchester City, who signed him for their academy, where he played for three years.

According to reports in Irish media, Nigerian football officials were keen on signing Bazunu to their national squad, but the player pledged allegiance to the country of his birth.

He has represented Ireland in 22 international fixtures over the past five years and wears the goalkeeper’s preferred number one shirt for the country.

What happened to Gavin Bazunu and what did he say?

Bazunu found himself at the centre of a row involving Ireland’s match against Israel , which is part of the Nations League competition held by European football’s governing body, UEFA.

After the FAI confirmed that it would participate in the match despite months-long calls for a boycott due to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, Bazunu became the only player to publicly opt out of the fixture.

He withdrew from both legs of the fixture, scheduled on Sunday in Debrecen, Hungary, and on October 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia. Bazunu has not participated in the squad’s training at the Nagyerdei Stadion since the team arrived in Hungary.

He posted a statement on his social media account confirming his withdrawal, saying:

“Representing my country means everything to me. I have the utmost respect for every single one of my teammates, the manager, his staff, and the Irish people.

However, I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly. I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle. Therefore, I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel.

My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong.

It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community, but against the atrocities in the region.

There are few times in life when you get a chance to stand up for something bigger, and I strongly believe that this is one of them.”

What has been the reaction to Bazunu’s decision?

Former Irish footballer and manager Brian Kerr voiced strong support for the goalkeeper and directed his anger towards the FAI for proceeding with the fixture despite months-long protests in Ireland.

“It’s a very legitimate position for him to take,” Kerr told Irish broadcaster Virgin Media Sport on Saturday. “It’s a heroic decision,” he said of Bazunu’s call.

The 73-year-old revealed his communication with the goalkeeper, saying Bazunu was “feeling quite low and shunned by some of the players and the FAI”.

“It has been suggested to him that it would be better if he left the squad, which I think is disgraceful because there’s a game against Austria to be played, and why shouldn’t he be involved in that game?”

Ireland play Austria on Thursday in their third Nations League game of the international football window.

Kerr also revealed that Bazunu was kept out of the FAI’s meeting with the players earlier on Saturday, when a vote was taken on the Israel game.

“He wasn’t involved in the vote. They presumed and they knew his vote and didn’t bring him into discussions, which is sad.”

Meanwhile, politicians, football fans, and Palestinian activists have also lauded Bazunu’s call to sit out of the game and go public with his sentiment.

“Well done to Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu for taking the principled decision to withdraw from the game against Israel,” said Jeremy Corbyn, former leader of the United Kingdom’s Labour Party.

“He should never have been put in this position, but he has shown immense moral courage and integrity by doing the right thing in the face of genocide,” Corbyn, who is a human rights and Palestinian rights advocate, wrote on X.

Sayeeda Warsi, British Muslim politician and Member of the UK’s House of Lords, commended Bazunu.

“Taking a principled stand is a hard decision to take but the easiest one to live with,” she wrote in a social media post.

Earlier this month, Mary Lou McDonald, leader of Ireland’s main opposition party, Sinn Fein, also called for the FAI to “do the right thing by its players” by telling them not to take the field.

Irish actor and pro-Palestine activist Liam Cunningham said the FAI and UEFA “passed the buck” on the row surrounding the fixture and lambasted their move to leave the decision to Bazunu.

“The man is a hero!” he said of the goalkeeper.

Palestinian activist and journalist Abubakr Abed said Bazunu’s stance “means the world to the players of Gaza”.

Ireland-based pro-Palestine rights group Irish Sport for Palestine termed the decision “a colossal failure” in a statement following Saturday’s confirmation.

“If they let this game go ahead, they will have let the bullies win. Symbolic gestures won’t cut it. The only acceptable action is to StopTheGame. There is still time to do the right thing. Ireland will support you.”

Who will replace Bazunu in Ireland’s squad?

While Caoimhin Kelleher and Max O’Leary are the other goalkeepers in Ireland’s squad, head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has named outfield defender Jimmy Dunne as one of two reserve goalkeepers since UEFA rules require three goalkeepers to be named in the squad.

Why and how did other Irish players decide to play against Israel?

Ireland began their UEFA Nations League 2026-27 campaign with a match against Kosovo on Thursday, following which the players and staff met in the capital, Pristina, to decide how they would approach the upcoming games against Israel.

It was agreed that players would travel to Debrecen ahead of the first leg.

On Saturday morning in Hungary, Ireland’s pre-match press conference was delayed by several hours due to continued team discussions.

The chief executive of the FAI, David Courell, later clarified that a player had “expressed their discomfort” about playing the game and intended to withdraw from the squad.

He also announced that players voted on whether to fulfil the two fixtures. Courell said the outcome was in favour of playing both games by a “significant majority”.

Following Ireland’s decision to fulfil the match, Israeli Football Association communications chief Shlomi Barzel said “football has won”.

Barzel commended the Irish federation for agreeing to go ahead with the game and stated that “separation between football and politics must be maintained”.

Why has the Irish public called for a boycott of the Israel game?

Ever since the fixture was first confirmed on February 12, the FAI has been under pressure to boycott the matches due to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Ireland’s status as a Palestine ally.

In May, leading Irish footballers joined celebrities in a campaign by Irish Sport for Palestine, urging Ireland to boycott the match against Israel. A United Nations inquiry confirmed in June 2025 that Israel was committing a genocide in Gaza .

The campaign group says Israel has breached UEFA and FIFA statutes by allowing teams to play on occupied Palestinian land and should be stripped of its membership at both football bodies.

How will Irish players show solidarity with Palestine?

As a result of team discussions, players decided on a range of actions to demonstrate their support for the Palestinian cause.

“There will be elements of the pre-match ceremony not be partaken in by the Republic of Ireland,” Courell said in his press conference, adding that his players will not partake in the traditional pre-match handshakes or exchange team pennants.

Exemption from media obligations for the remainder of the international break has also been requested by the players.

They will pay tribute to “all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict” by wearing black armbands.

A significant proportion of match fees from the upcoming games against Israel and Austria will be donated to charitable causes.

What’s behind Ireland’s support for Palestine?

A shared sense of struggle underpins the bond , with Dublin making landmark diplomatic moves against Israel in the past few years and especially during the Gaza genocide.

In the West, Ireland has been home to some of the loudest criticism of Israel and support of Palestinian rights .

After Israel began striking Gaza in October 2023, the Republic of Ireland, a member of the European Union, was one of the first countries to call for an “immediate humanitarian ceasefire” to meet the “urgent” needs of civilians.

In 1980, Ireland was the first European country to call for the establishment of a Palestinian state. Thirteen years later, it became the last EU member to open an Israeli embassy in Dublin, which Israel subsequently shuttered in 2024 in response to Irish protests over the Gaza war.

In 2021, Ireland became the first EU country to declare that Israel was involved in the “de facto annexation” of Palestinian land, upsetting Israel’s Foreign Ministry, which said the move “constitutes a victory for extremist Palestinian factions”.

“Ireland’s own history of colonisation by the British has made many Irish people empathetic towards other nations under occupation or colonisation,” said Cathal O’hEanna, a representative of the left-wing nationalist party Sinn Fein.

“Our centuries-long struggle for the right to self-determination resonates with the Palestinian struggle for statehood and independence,” he told Al Jazeera.

In June, Ireland barred Israel’s National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and its Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich from visiting the country, citing their conduct towards pro-Palestinian activists and support for policies that would displace Palestinians from their homeland.

Earlier this month, Ireland became the second country, after the Netherlands, to announce a boycott of next year’s Eurovision Song Contest over Israel’s participation.

Irish rap group Kneecap’s members – who rap in Gaeilge, the Irish language, as well as English – have been outspoken in their condemnation of Israel’s genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

Kneecap’s Liam O’Hanna was charged in May of last year with displaying a Hezbollah flag during a November 2024 concert in London, in violation of the United Kingdom’s 2000 Terrorism Act. The rap group called the attempted prosecution a “British state witch-hunt”.

Speaking after the British prosecutors lost an appeal seeking to reinstate a “terrorism” charge against him in March, O’Hanna, also known as Liam Og O hAnnaid, said that the case was “never about me, never about any threat to the public and never about terrorism”.

“It was always about Palestine ,” he said, “about what happens if you dare to speak up, about what happens if you can reach large groups of people and expose their hypocrisy, about the lengths Britain will go to cover up Israeli and US war crimes.”

articles.title: Luna Rossa también gana en Nápoles mientras Botín y Trittel acaban terceros con La Roche-Posay
articles.standfirst: Pese a que el equipo francés, del que los españoles son el 50%, volcó dos veces en la segunda regata preliminar
articles.summary: Pese a que el equipo francés, del que los españoles son el 50%, volcó dos veces en la segunda regata preliminar
articles.body: Era la primera vez que la flota de la Copa América, que se celebrará a partir de mayo de 2027, competía en aguas de Nápoles. Aunque lo hizo a bordo de los AC40, la segunda preliminar de la 38 edición ha servido como acercamiento al campo de regatas en el que se examinarán el año que viene con los AC75. Al igual que sucedió en la primera en Cagliari, el Luna Rossa italiano sigue siendo profeta en su tierra y se coronó campeón tras ganar en la final al Emirates Team New Zealand, vigente defensor. Peter Burling, ahora como patrón del equipo italiano, volvió a ganar la partida a sus excompañeros. La buena noticia para España es que Diego Botín y Florian Trittel, el 50% del equipo francés La Roche-Posay Racing Team y vigentes campeones olímpicos, fueron terceros pese a los dos volcadas que sufrieron a lo largo del fin de semana. Mejoran un puesto respecto a la cita anterior en Cerdeña. El viernes, unas condiciones meteorológicas inestables redujeron el programa a dos mangas. Quentin Delapierre, Diego Botín, Jason Saunders y Florian Trittel lograron una sexta plaza en la primera. En la salida de la segunda, el AC40 francés volcó y el equipo tuvo que retirarse. Los cuatro tripulantes resultaron ilesos. El sábado lo comenzaron con un sexto puesto. Se llevaron la victoria en la siguiente manga, pero en la tercera del día llegó otro susto. En la última trasluchada hacia la meta, cuando iban líderes, el AC40 volcó de nuevo. Pudieron tomar la salida y en la última certificaron su segundo triunfo del día. Y cerró el domingo con un tercer y un segundo puesto. Con un total de 48 puntos después de ocho mangas, a solo 8 de Emirates Team New Zealand, la tripulación fue la mejor de los mortales, ya que Luna Rossa y Emirates hoy en día están en otro nivel. "Hacemos un balance positivo porque como equipo hemos demostrado muchas cosas este fin de semana. Sobre todo, cómo sabemos trabajar tanto en el agua como en tierra con el trabajo que ha hecho nuestro equipo de tierra por la noche tras las volcadas y recuperar todo al 100% para el día siguiente. Y a nivel de mentalidad hemos podido salir y hacer casi un día prácticamente inmejorable. Esto refleja muy bien dónde estamos. No hemos terminado dos pruebas pero el resultado ha sido mejor que el de Cagliari (fueron cuartos), así que claramente la curva es ascendente, y nos da motivación y energía que nos llevamos de cara a los próximos meses de trabajo de invierno muy duro", reconoce Trittel, trimmer del equipo francés. "Es muy bueno haber demostrado que, a pesar de haber tenido imprevistos duros, nos hemos recuperado muy bien. Es algo que indica que somos un equipo fuerte en ese aspecto y es muy importante de cara a futuras competiciones", añade Botín, que ejerce de copatrón. Los regatistas españoles explican que han mejorado en las salidas y que han entendido mejor cómo regatear, moverse en el campo de regatas y la comunicación entre los tripulantes. También cómo se comporta el viento. Todo ello será la base para trabajar este invierno en Nápoles. Porque la tripulación y el resto del equipo de La Roche-Posay ya se instaló allí desde principios de mes, concretamente en la zona de Bagnoli. Esta misma semana han recibido el AC75 con el que se entrenarán a partir de ahora en aguas napolitanas. Italia nunca ha ganado la Jarra de las Cien Guineas. Para cumplir el sueño de lograrlo en casa fichó a Peter Burling, el Messi del mar. Con él como patrón, el Emirates Team New Zealand ganó las tres últimas Copas América. En Cagliari, el neozelandés se estrenó con el equipo italiano con victoria. En Nápoles volvió a coronarse y a presentar su candidatura a ser el Desafío que rete a los 'Kiwis' en julio del año que viene. Pese a que la tripulación era completamente distinta a la que compitió en Cagliari, Luna Rossa llegó a la última jornada como líder de la clasificación y confirmó su posición después de las dos últimas regatas de flota. En la final ante el equipo neozelandés, segundo tras las regatas de flota, Burling y Marco Gradoni como timoneles y Gianluigi Ugolini y Maria Giubilei como trimmers se llevó la victoria. Los resultados de las regatas preliminares no otorgan puntos para la competición principal. La Copa Louis Vuitton de la 38ª Copa del América de Nápoles, de la que saldrá el barco que rete al Defensor, se disputará del 10 al 18 de julio de 2027. Será la primera vez que Italia sea sede de la prueba, que toma el relevo de Barcelona, donde se disputó la anterior edición.

articles.title: Why the New Orleans Saints can cover the spread against the Las Vegas Raiders in NFL Week 3
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders face the New Orleans Saints in Week 3 as both teams look to prove their early-season success wasn't a fluke against each other.
articles.body: Each NFL season has its own story and uniqueness. Discovering it is part of the fun, but it can also be a point of contention when you’re a sports bettor. You don’t have a ton of time to determine who is a good team and who is bad. You have to constantly evaluate and change your opinions on things. I’ve already changed my opinion on both of these teams – the Raiders and the Saints, and now they face each other in Week 3. The Las Vegas Raiders cost me some money last week, or maybe I should say the Chargers cost me money once again. After backing them in Week 1, I took the Chargers to beat them in Week 2 and cover the spread. The Raiders looked like a fairly well-oiled machine against Los Angeles, getting three touchdown passes from Kirk Cousins on 19-for-29 passing. Part of the key for the Raiders will be keeping Cousins upright, and he was only sacked twice. The other key to the Raiders' success is getting Ashton Jeanty to effectively run the ball. What I liked about the Raiders game is that despite him not having a very good game, they stuck with it. Jeanty had just 48 yards on 21 attempts. He did haul in four of his seven targets, but added just 15 yards. Before we crown the Raiders as being elite, let’s realize that the Chargers were also part of their problem. Sure, some of this can be attributed to Las Vegas, but Los Angeles fumbling six times was also ridiculous. The New Orleans Saints have put together some decent games to start their season. They almost came back and beat the Lions in Week 1 after bringing them to overtime. In the first two quarters of the season, the Saints scored zero total points. Since about the middle of the third quarter of that game, they have scored 54 points. All of their touchdowns have come through the air as well, relying on Tyler Shough to lead the way. If you want to get even more granular with the team, to see where the struggles and successes have been, let’s take a look at Week 2. The Saints have scored six total points in the first half of the two games. In the fourth quarter and overtime, they’ve scored 40 points. Maybe it is Shough taking too long to figure out opposing defenses. Maybe there is some other reason, but they are playing with fire by waiting until the last quarter to try and come back. The Saints have played two rather difficult teams and now get to play at home. The Raiders had an easy game to open the season, and their second game wasn’t exactly a challenge considering how bad the Chargers look. Again, some of that was certainly self-inflicted, but I don’t want to take a ton away from the Raiders. I just don’t think this is a great situation for the Raiders. I don’t think their offense will be able to be quite as effective in this one. I like the Saints to win and cover the -3 spread. articles.title: Mr. Olympia 2026 Final Results, Top Videos and Predictions for 2027 Event
articles.summary: The 2026 Mr. Olympia brought one of the more tightly contested Open competitions we've seen in recent memory. Nick Walker rallied from last year's sixth-place finish to claim the Sandow Trophy, but several other contenders were in the mix during Saturday's finals.
articles.body:
The 2026 Mr. Olympia brought one of the more tightly contested Open competitions we've seen in recent memory. Nick Walker rallied from last year's sixth-place finish to claim the Sandow Trophy, but several other contenders were in the mix during Saturday's finals.

Reigning champion Derek Lunsford, 2026 Arnold Classic winner Andrew Jacked, and 2024 Mr. Olympia Samson Dauda were seen as obvious threats by the end of Friday's prejudging.

Lunsford appeared to be in championship form and quite capable of claiming his third Sandow Trophy in four years. Jacked and Dauda, meanwhile, set themselves apart with sheer size.

Dauda may have even been in better form than he was during his 2024 championship run.

However, Walker's conditioning, refined physique, and terrific finals routine earned him the top spot and his biggest win as an IFBB pro.

While we might have easily seen a different result on a different night, Walker believes that he beat out all of the top contenders were in their best shape.

Dauda finished a close second, and while he certainly would have enjoyed winning his second Sandow in three years, he was happy with his finish. He noted after the competition that he learned from last year's fourth-place slide and dialed things in for Saturday.

Lunsford did not successfully defend his title, but he still had a strong routine and managed to finish in the top three. Jacked didn't appear to be quite as sharp as he was in Columbus for the Arnold Classic earlier in the year. However, he still brought an impressive blend of size and conditioning.

Tonio Burton rounded out the top five and was the final prize-money winner.

Is it too early for Walker, Dauda, and the other top competitors to begin looking ahead to next year's IFBB season? Of course not, and we could see even more prize money on the line in 2027.

The Arnold Classic raised its top prize to $750,000 this year. While the Olympia did not follow suit, it may raise the payout for 2027. Regardless, Walker will be looking to become the first repeat champion since Mamdouh Elssbiay won in 2020 and 2021.

We'll probably have a better idea of who the top 2027 Olympia competitors are after the Arnold Classic, which has become the consensus No. 2 IFBB competition after the Olympia. However, it'll be a massive surprise if Walker, Dauda, Lunsford, and Jacked aren't the four favorites once again.

The prediction here is that Dauda finds an even better balance between mass and leanness for a championship frame that puts him back on top.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys call about potential trade for disgruntled Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys spent a considerable amount of their resources in an effort to improve their defense during the course of the offseason. They hired a new...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys spent a considerable amount of their resources in an effort to improve their defense during the course of the offseason. They hired a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker , traded for pass rusher Rashan Gary , and drafted defensive back Caleb Downs with the 11th overall pick.

Unfortunately for Dallas, their multiple attempts at building a better defense have not had the results they hoped for early in 2026. At 1-1, there are still some aspects of the unit that are desperate need of improvement.

Among these is the secondary, where the Cowboys are starting to call about one disgruntled Pittsburgh Steelers star.

The Dallas Cowboys have called the Pittsburgh Steelers about Joey Porter Jr.

Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is one of the most popular players on their team. The son of a franchise legend, he is in an awkward situation with the organization when it comes to his contract. For as long as anyone can remember, Pittsburgh does not negotiate contracts with players during the regular season. When the Steelers and Porter were unable to come to a contract extension agreement during the offseason, the organization cut off talks.

This has led many to believe that 2026 will be Porter's final season with the Steelers. He has yet to play this year due to a back injury and his ramp-up as a result. Some believe this is a tactic by the defensive star to get the organization to resume talking to his agent regarding his contract.

Obviously, this is not an ideal situation, and some believe that Pittsburgh could end up trading Porter before the deadline. One of the teams that has called about him is the Cowboys, according to ESPN :

"A handful of teams, including the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions , have begun making inquiries about the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., league sources told ESPN. "The Steelers would be willing to listen to trade offers for Porter, according to sources, but they would want a strong compensation package if they were to deal the fourth-year star. "Porter has been seeking a new contract, but the Steelers do not negotiate deals during the season, raising questions about the possibility of a trade."

articles.title: “Brought it Home for You”: Dylan Raiola Shares Heartfelt Message for Dante Moore after Oregon QB Carted Off with Scary Injury
articles.summary: When Dylan Raiola transferred to Oregon from Nebraska in January, many believed he would be the new QB1. However, when Dante Moore decided not to go to the N...
articles.body:
When Dylan Raiola transferred to Oregon from Nebraska in January, many believed he would be the new QB1. However, when Dante Moore decided not to go to the NFL yet, Raiola did not become the starter as many had expected. As the two played together at Oregon, though, they have formed a friendship, and when Moore got knocked out cold after a hard hit from USC defenders, the Ducks QB2 shared a heartfelt message on his Instagram story.

"Love you 5! Got your back fam! We brought it home for you!" he wrote in his caption.

It was Raiola who carried Oregon past USC after Moore got hit hard by USC linebacker Desman Stephens, with the Ducks winning 41-27 in the process. One of his biggest highlights was when he threw a touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore to break the deadlock against the Trojans.

As for Dante Moore, play was paused for around 11 minutes as his teammates rushed to his side to make sure he was OK. He then received medical attention and left the game by ambulance. The linebacker who hit him, Desman Stephens, was then ejected for targeting.

Dante Moore will get at least one more week of rest, as the Ducks will have a bye next week. They will then head back home to Eugene, where they host the UCLA Bruins on Oct. 10. Whether or not the Ducks QB1 will be starting the game is still in question.

Oregon Coach Dan Lanning Calls Hit on Dante Moore 'Disgusting'

After the game, Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning expressed his thoughts on the way USC linebacker Desman Stephens hit Dante Moore, calling it "disgusting" and saying he wants the USC player to learn something from that situation.

"It's a disgusting play," Lanning said. "We don't want to see it happen. It's disappointing that it happened. I'm praying that our player's healthy, and I'm praying that their player can learn from that situation."

For now, Moore remains in the hospital but is now able to move, according to Lanning.

As for Stephens, he is facing mounting criticism for his behavior after Dante Moore was sent to the hospital. He was "disqualified" from the game but was seen on the sidelines during the second half, where he was smiling and laughing with his teammates.

articles.title: Stella Calls for “Common Sense” After Colapinto Starts Another Social Media Storm
articles.summary: Andrea Stella calls for common sense from F1 drivers after Franco Colapinto wiped out Alpine teammate and Lando Norris at the Azerbaijan GP. A disappointed M...
articles.body:
Andrea Stella calls for common sense from F1 drivers after Franco Colapinto wiped out Alpine teammate and Lando Norris at the Azerbaijan GP.

A disappointed McLaren's Norris called for a race ban for drivers causing incidents like in F1 Azerbaijan GP , which his rivals did not agree readily . Even team boss Stella did not readily align with the thought, but raised the common sense topic from experienced drivers.

He thought circuits like Baku always throw challenges like what happened at Turn 1. It is a common theme at restarts which drivers are aware and mindful of, which is why he felt whether Colapinto or anyone else, should have applied common sense in tackling tricky conditions.

Stella Fears Briatore Penalty will be Harsher for Colapinto

In terms of the penalty, he put full faith in the FIA stewards to handle the topic and didn't know if repercussions from Alpine F1 chief Flavio Briatore would be harsher or the penalty for Colapinto. The stewards handed him a 5-place grid drop, but the Italian was certainly harsher in the press release.

He said there would be consequences which raised social media theories about dropping Colapinto from racing in Malaysia – something he can do like he did with Jack Doohan previously. "Well, look, it's a complex matter," said Stella to the media, when asked his view on the topic.

"I guess this is being reviewed by the stewards as we speak pretty much. I'm sure it will be reviewed by Flavio as well. I'm not sure which one is going to be harsher for whoever caused the problem. I think independently of the discussion that you can have because of the penalty.

Stella Recalls How Tricky Baku Circuit Usually Is

"I think when you drive a Formula 1 and you are approaching corner one in Baku and you have seen so many videos of the past, you just should be capitalising on this experience that you should be having as a Formula 1 driver because there's consequence in this case which I sure I'm sure is a shame for Alpine, for both drivers and there's a shame for and there's a penalty for other drivers.

"So I think definitely the penalty should take into account that there's some circuits in which you have to use extra prudency and there's an full history of problems that happened like this especially in a street circuit where there's no way to use the run off area to somehow mitigate the consequences of somebody running onto you.

"So we trust the stewards, their approach but above all we should trust the drivers that they apply a certain degree of just common sense, I would say while driving," summed up Stella, as social media furor kicked-off against Norris on social media, following the Brit's statement.

It forced Alpine to release a statement on Sunday afternoon to ease the tensions. Colapinto was already apologetic about the incident post-race, while Pierre Gasly accepted it but needed a day to cool off, considering the huge points loss for the F1 team in the battle against Racing Bulls.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz states how important the Laver Cup is to him, ‘I love playing’
articles.summary: Team Europe are champions of the world once again, having triumphed on the third day of the Laver Cup. In the end, it was Alexander...
articles.body:
Team Europe are champions of the world once again, having triumphed on the third day of the Laver Cup.

In the end, it was Alexander Zverev who secured the trophy, snatching it back from Andre Agassi's Rest of the World team.

His win over Learner Tien meant that a third match was not needed on the Sunday, and Carlos Alcaraz was stood down, much to the disappointment of a hopeful crowd in the O2.

In all honesty, the Spaniard was likely relieved to not have to take to the court, given how hard-fought yesterday's win over Taylor Fritz was.

Alcaraz will now seek to rest that wrist after a hectic return to action following five months out, and he spoke at his press conference about how events like the Laver Cup fit into an already-packed schedule that has garnered criticism from him recently.

Carlos Alcaraz claims the Laver Cup brings joy back to his tennis

There's no denying that the 23-year-old is perhaps the most universally liked player tennis has right now.

So, to have gone without him for so long marked a hammer blow for the ATP Tour, particularly given the lack of young marketable stars who stepped up in his absence.

Alas, Alcaraz is back, and with him has come an energy and buzz that has certainly been missing.

His unrivalled joy for the sport is infectious, and responding to a question posed by Tennishead at his Team Europe championship press conference, he reiterated that notion when discussing the schedule and his decision to play the Laver Cup.

Asked about his complaints about the schedule and feeling burnt out, it was Zverev who spoke first, claiming: "You feel burnt out? You had a four-month vacation."

"I know, but you have to speak out sometimes," Alcaraz said with a smile, to which Zverev then joked: "I played 98 matches since you've been gone."

Alcaraz then started: "No, I said it since the beginning of the week. You know, you've got to use everything to your favour, and I'm using, for example, this tournament to bring my joy back. I love playing.

"You know, every time that I step on the court, I love it, because I'm doing with these guys, when it is a team event is totally different, playing for your side, for your teammates, playing for the guys who are supporting you from the bench, from outside. And that's great.

"Obviously having a great captain and co-captain behind you all the time, it's great. This week, as I said, I just really wanted to — I mean, I just love to be part of it and makes me find my joy when I'm playing, help me a lot to find my great tennis when I'm playing out there, and help me a lot to the next tournament.

"So that's what these kind of events brings to me."

Carlos Alcaraz's record vs Alex de Minaur had the Laver Cup wrapped up

Had Tien sparked a successful comeback vs Zverev, or Team Europe lost the doubles, Alcaraz would have been called into action to face De Minaur.

For the Aussie, only survival would have been on the cards, whilst the seven-time Grand Slam champion would have been chasing glory.

Carlos Alcaraz's head-to-head record vs Alex de Minaur

He has form in confidently claiming silverware, and despite recording an impressive win over the new Roland Garros and US Open champion yesterday, Alcaraz would have been a different beast altogether.

It's worth noting that De Minaur has never beaten the generational talent in six attempts.

The Giants force another 3-and-out as Jevon Holland comes out of nowhere to punch the ball out of Wan'Dale Robinson's hands.

The Giants fail to convert another 3rd down, but Jordan Stout hits a BOOMING 73-yard punt to flip the field. The Titans commit a holding penalty to back themselves up even more.

The Giants force another 3-and-out, with the Giants' pass rush pressuring Cam Ward and forcing a poor throw.

Another miscue from the Giants as Cam Skattebo and Jameis Winston collide in the backfield. The Giants will punt after a 3-and-out.

The Giants force a 3-and-out after Wan'Dale Robinson's progress is called stopped. He continued to churn his legs and was close to the first down marker, but the play isn't reviewable.

The Giants' drive stalls around the 25-yard line ends in a Dominic Zvada field goal. Giants lead the Titans 3-0.

The Jameis-coaster is in full effect. After nearly throwing an interception, Winston finds Cam Skattebo way downfield for a first down.

Brian Burns gets on the field on 3rd and 6, and the Giants knock the ball away from Wan'Dale Robinson to force a 3-and-out.

The Giants fail to score after getting great field position from the fumble. They can't recover after the penalty and punt the ball away.

The Giants get the ball on the 37-yard line after recovering the fumble, keeping the ball on the ground.

The Giants win the opening coin toss and will defer. The Titans will receive the opening kick-off… And steal the opening possession after forcing a fumble!
